shared_elements: upright monolithic anthropomorphic form carved in low relief
horizontal band/register running across the upper part of the body
row of repeated curved loop/arch-like signs
band of short parallel strokes or zigzag as a filler register
ring/curved motifs on the body surface
arm/limb elements rendered in shallow relief on the body
justification: Both are standing monolithic quasi-human forms whose surfaces carry shallow relief organised into horizontal registers, with a row of repeated curved loop/arch signs and a band of short parallel strokes above ring-like motifs and a belt-like band, plus limbs rendered flat against the body. The decisive difference is content below those bands: B is populated by recognisable animals in profile (a predator-like quadruped, birds, a snake-like sinuous form) interacting with the pillar's body, whereas A carries only abstract rings, spirals and arm/hand forms with no creatures at all.
